title: K-Electric Bill Calculator 2026 (Karachi Tariff) | Wattlyst
meta: Estimate your K-Electric bill from units with the current tariff, FCA and taxes. Protected and non-protected slabs explained.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: What is the K-Electric per unit rate?
p: K-Electric used to have its own tariff schedule, but NEPRA's 2026 determination rationalised it to the uniform A-1 domestic rates charged across Pakistan. An unprotected Karachi home is billed the rate of the slab its monthly units reach on every unit: 300 units at Rs 33.10 here, less for the lower slabs and most for the open-ended top slab. Protected and lifeline consumers have their own low rates.

The examples and table below print the rate for each slab from the tariff file. The month's FCA, which K-Electric adds or subtracts per unit, is the one line that is not in the uniform tariff; it is the same national figure NEPRA sets for the other DISCOs, pre-filled here with the latest NEPRA-verified month, so replace it with your bill's.

sections.h2: What is the K-Electric tariff for 2026?
p: The tariff is the uniform domestic schedule notified as SRO 279(I)/2026: two lifeline slabs up to 100 units, two protected slabs up to 200 units, unprotected slabs of 100 units each up to 700 and one open-ended slab above. Each slab carries its own fixed charge per kW of sanctioned load, and connections of 5 kW and above are billed on peak and off-peak ToU rates instead.

On top of the energy and fixed charges, the bill adds the FC surcharge, the quarterly tariff adjustment, the monthly FCA and GST. The surcharge, QTA and GST defaults here come from secondary sources and change over time, and how GST and the FC surcharge apply to lifeline bills is still being verified, so copy those lines from your bill.

sections.h2: KE bill calculator vs the official K-Electric bill
p: This KE bill calculator estimates the bill from your units and category. It cannot see your account, arrears, the exact FCA for the month or any local charge, so treat the result as a planning estimate and as a check on the slab you were billed in. Your official bill, duplicate bill and payment status are on the K-Electric website.

The full electricity bill calculator for Pakistan explains the slabs and the protected check in more depth; the maths is the same. The FCA line works like the FPA on other bills; see what the FPA line on your bill means.

faq.q: How do I get a K-Electric bill estimate from my units?
faq.a: Enter the units and sanctioned load from the bill, tick protected only if the bill says so, and replace the pre-filled FCA with the one on your bill in the advanced fields. For 300 units the estimate is Rs 14,186, FCA included.

faq.q: What is the K-Electric per unit rate for a home?
faq.a: The uniform NEPRA domestic slab rate for the slab your month reaches: Rs 33.10 per unit for an unprotected home using 300 units. The table above lists the rate for every slab; protected and lifeline consumers pay less.

faq.q: Is the K-Electric tariff for 2026 higher than other DISCOs?
faq.a: No. The 2026 determination rationalised K-Electric's domestic tariff to the same uniform rates as the ex-WAPDA DISCOs. NEPRA applies the same monthly FCA to K-Electric consumers as the FPA on other DISCOs' bills, so the same units give the same bill; real bills differ only by billing days, arrears and local items.

faq.q: Does this KE bill calculator include the FCA?
faq.a: Yes. It is pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified FCA, the one for July 2026. The FCA changes every month and can be a credit, so copy the per-unit figure from your bill into the FCA field under advanced settings and the estimate uses it.

faq.q: How many units keep a K-Electric consumer protected?
faq.a: At or under 200 units in every one of the last 6 months on a connection below 5 kW. One month over the limit moves the home to unprotected rates on every unit.

Karachi and the nearby areas of Sindh and Balochistan it supplies, such as Hub and Uthal in Lasbela; the rest of Balochistan is QESCO's. K-Electric's own call centre is also 118, open around the clock, and the duplicate bill is on the K-Electric website.

faq.q: Where do I see my official K-Electric bill?
faq.a: On the K-Electric website, using the account or consumer number printed on the bill. This calculator does not fetch your bill; it estimates one from the units you enter.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: K-Electric's domestic tariff was rationalised to the same uniform NEPRA A-1 rates as the ex-WAPDA DISCOs in the 2026 determination, so a Karachi bill for a given number of units matches a Lahore or Islamabad bill, fuel charge adjustment included: NEPRA applies the same FCA to K-Electric.
The K-Electric per unit rate for an unprotected home using 300 units is Rs 33.10 on every unit, giving Rs 9,930 in energy charges before the fixed charge, surcharges, FCA and GST.
FCA is K-Electric's name for the monthly fuel charge adjustment that other DISCOs print as FPA; it changes every month, can be a credit, and is the field to copy from your bill.
A K-Electric protected consumer is one whose last 6 bills were all at or under 200 units on a connection below 5 kW; such bills are worked out slab-wise at the low protected rates.

The bill jumps at 700 units: up to there every unit is billed at Rs 41.85, but one unit more moves all of them to the top slab rate of Rs 47.20, which adds Rs 4,481 to the bill of an unprotected 1 kW home.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Expecting a separate K-Electric rate. Since the 2026 rationalisation the slab rates are the uniform NEPRA domestic rates; the FCA is the same national figure too, which NEPRA applies to K-Electric under the Federal Government's policy guidelines for a uniform FCA.
Keeping the pre-filled FCA when your bill shows a different one. The fuel charge adjustment is often the line that makes two months with the same units cost different amounts; enter your bill's rate.
Ticking protected on a low month. Protection needs all of the last six months under the limit, and a Karachi summer bill with an AC usually breaks the run.
Dividing the bill total by units to find the rate. Fixed charge, surcharges and GST are inside the total; the slab rate is the energy line divided by units.

fields.label: Units on the K-Electric bill
fields.hint: Units (kWh) for the month, from the bill or from this and last month's meter readings.

fields.name: sanctioned_kw
fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed on the bill; most Karachi homes are one to five. It sets the fixed charge. A connection of 5 kW or more is billed on peak and off-peak (ToU) rates instead: use the ToU bill calculator.

fields.name: protected
fields.label: Protected consumer
fields.hint: Tick if every one of your last six K-Electric bills was within the protected unit limit; the bill prints the category.

fields.name: lifeline
fields.label: Lifeline consumer (up to one hundred units)
fields.hint: Only for very small consumers whose bill shows the lifeline category.

fields.name: period
fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from the bill. Secondary-source default.
fields.placeholder: Blank = Rs 3.23 per unit (none on lifeline)

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FCA (fuel charge adjustment)
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for July 2026 charged on September 2026 bills. October 2026 bills carry Rs 1.11 per unit for August 2026, reported in the news; this page keeps the latest NEPRA-verified rate until that decision is published. Replace it with the FCA rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit). Protected homes pay it too; lifeline bills carry none.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

examples.text: 100 units at the lifeline rate of Rs 7.74 = Rs 774, with no fixed charge, no QTA and no FPA. With the FC surcharge and GST fields blank the estimate assumes neither applies to lifeline bills (still being verified): Rs 774.

content.answer: A Karachi home on K-Electric using 300 units a month as an unprotected consumer with a 1 kW connection pays about Rs 14,186: Rs 9,930 energy charge at Rs 33.10 per unit, plus fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, the July 2026 FCA and GST. K-Electric bill = units × slab rate + fixed charge + adjustments + GST.

formula.text: Bill = units × slab rate + fixed Rs/kW × sanctioned kW + (FC + QTA + FCA) × units, then + GST
lines: slab rate = rate of the band the month's units reach (unprotected) or slab-wise (protected)
fixed = Rs per kW of the band reached × sanctioned kW
FC = financing cost surcharge; QTA = quarterly adjustment; FCA = K-Electric's monthly fuel charge adjustment
